title: 5b brainstorm: component discovery + vocabulary design
description:
Brainstorm the component discovery and vocabulary layers using vidhi-brainstorm. Key areas:

- Graph clustering approach (Louvain/Leiden on call/dependency graph) — algorithm choice, stability across edits, performance on real codebases
- Component identity and lifecycle — how do components survive recomputation? Merge/split/drift tracking. Stable IDs.
- Component lifecycle state (sketching vs stable) — how this interacts with convention enforcement
- Semantic anchors — identifying load-bearing types/functions per component via graph centrality
- Concept density — metric for review prioritization (dense = needs more human attention)
- Vocabulary layer (L5) — mapping human concepts to code locations: auto-computed labels, human aliases (.sutra/aliases.toml), fuzzy matching via HRR embed-mode vectors
- Auto-learning from agent sessions — should concept mappings learn automatically or only accept explicit aliases?
- How components compose with the adapter trait interface from 5a — do language adapters declare component-relevant capabilities?
- Storage model — components as durable entities (they carry human intent via names, lifecycle state, aliases)

Input: docs/sutra-vision.md (L1 + L5 sections), docs/sutra-architecture.md, phase 4 spike results (if any), 5a decisions
Output: shared understanding ready for PRD
decisions: Louvain on file-level call/dependency graph with 1/ambiguity weighting. Single-level sufficient. Resolution parameter auto-tuned with human override via .sutra/components.toml. HRR edge reweighting deferred to post-v1.
Recompute clustering lazily: triggered on first query after staleness detected. Stale when (a) files added/removed, or (b) >10% of inter-file edges changed since last clustering run.

Components are durable entities (UUID, name, lifecycle, timestamps). component_membership is ephemeral (recomputed from clustering). Reconciliation via Jaccard overlap: >0.6 overlap → match to existing component; no match → create new; no matching cluster → mark dissolved with timestamp.
Component events (merge, split, drift) are durable and surfaced in review reports. Merge = two components collapsed. Split = one became two. Drift = >30% file shift between components.
Lifecycle state is per-component (sketching | stable), not per-file. Sketching flattens conventions to informational; constraints still enforced.

Semantic anchors identified by: high in-degree within component, betweenness centrality, git stability, naming alignment. 3-7 per component. Stored as ephemeral (recomputed from graph metrics). Used for orient (start-here pointers), review (anchor-modified = deeper inspection), drift detection.

Concept density built in v1. Initial metric from Layer 0 data: (unique symbol kinds × naming stem diversity) / LOC. Richer FCA-based version (unique attribute combinations / total symbols) comes when 5c convention system lands.
Vocabulary layer (L5): human aliases via .sutra/aliases.toml (highest trust), component names, semantic anchor names, HRR embed-mode fuzzy matching (lowest trust). aliases table is durable.
No auto-learning from agent sessions in v1. Explicit aliases only. Auto-learning deferred until there's a curation/review UX for proposed mappings.
Component auto-naming: longest common path prefix of member files, stripped to last segment. Fallback: most-central file's parent directory. Human can rename anytime (durable).
Dissolved components: kept in DB marked dissolved with timestamp, hidden from normal queries. Aliases pointing at them become orphaned (surfaced in reconciliation report). No silent deletion.

Adapters provide module_boundary_hints() — tells clustering how much to weight the language's own module structure vs purely structural clustering. Rust mod = strong boundary prior; Python packages = mild hint; C directories = weak signal.
Storage: components (durable), component_membership (ephemeral), aliases (durable), semantic_anchors (ephemeral), component_events (durable).
